title: Volume of a slab intersected with a ball: Lᵐ ≤ 2r(2R)^{m−1}
statement: Let m ∈ ℕ, let ν, c ∈ ℝᵐ with |ν| = 1, and let r, R ∈ ℝ. Then Lᵐ({w ∈ ℝᵐ : |⟨w − c, ν⟩| ≤ r and |w − c| ≤ R}) ≤ ofReal(2r·(2R)^{m−1}), i.e. the volume of the slab of half-width r normal to ν, intersected with the closed ball of radius R about c, is at most max(0, 2r(2R)^{m−1}). Notation: ℝ^d = Rn d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) with Euclidean norm |·| and inner product ⟨·,·⟩; Lᵈ = volume on ℝ^d (applied to an arbitrary set it is the Lebesgue outer measure); Hˢ = μHE[s] (Euclidean-normalized Hausdorff outer measure) and μH[s] the unnormalized Hausdorff measure; diam = Metric.ediam (extended diameter in [0,∞]); DF(u) = fderiv ℝ F u with the operator norm ‖·‖; ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal; natural-number subtraction m − 1.
lean_statement: ∀ (m : ℕ) (ν c : Rn m) (r R : ℝ), ‖ν‖ = 1 → volume {w : Rn m | |inner ℝ (w - c) ν| ≤ r ∧ ‖w - c‖ ≤ R} ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (2 * r * (2 * R) ^ (m - 1))
